done_when: Git merges plans/roadmap.json itself: forge sync registers a merge rule that keeps both sides' new items and the latest status of each, so two branches that each add an item merge without a conflict; a test merges two such branches

findings.body: `forge sync` registers the driver only in the local clone’s Git config. Forge’s actual merge path calls `gh pr merge --squash` (`src/forge/merge.py:64`), so GitHub cannot run that locally configured driver. After one PR adds a roadmap item, a second PR adding another item can still have a roadmap conflict on GitHub. The new test exercises a local `git merge`, so it does not catch this gap. Git documents that [custom drivers are defined in local Git config](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes); GitHub [blocks PR merges with unresolved conflicts](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/merge-conflicts). Resolve and push the roadmap merge before the PR merge, and test that flow.
findings.title: Not done: Git merges plans/roadmap.json itself for PRs that each add an item

findings.body: The driver selects an entire item from one side based on status rank. For example, if ours updates an existing item’s title while theirs changes its status from `pending` to `done`, this condition copies theirs and silently discards the title edit. Merge independent fields separately, or leave incompatible edits as a conflict.
findings.title: Preserve independent edits when choosing an item's later status

why: plans/roadmap.json conflicts on almost every merge, because every story and fix appends to it
